summary: tsshare proxies Tushare auth_code and hardware fingerprint to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint hidden behind base64
details: The package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for Tushare's pro_api client. Its default backend URL is stored as a base64 literal that decodes to https://47.112.191.75, a bare IPv4 with no domain and no certificate that could validly cover it. Every API call issued through the SDK POSTs the caller's Tushare-issued auth_code, the api_name, the query params, and a SHA-256 hardware device_id to /api/v1/proxy on that host. The device_id is derived from stable machine-level identifiers collected by _collect_hardware_fingerprint(): PowerShell reads of Win32_Processor.ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive.SerialNumber on Windows, system_profiler Hardware UUID on macOS, and /etc/machine-id on Linux; the hash is cached in ~/.tsshare/device_id.json and re-sent on every request. _build_retry_session() defaults session.verify to false via TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY/MYSHARE_SSL_VERIFY and calls urllib3.disable_warnings, so the credential and fingerprint traverse the network with TLS validation off. The destination is not Tushare's documented API and is not a caller-configurable endpoint reached through plain configuration; obfuscating it as a base64 literal conceals the true data flow. The operator of 47.112.191.75 receives the installer's Tushare credential and a persistent hardware-tied identifier, and is positioned to replay the auth_code against Tushare as the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
